show: Who Did What Now With Katie Charlwood
titel: 205. Unit 731 - Japan's Covert Human Experimentation Program

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen (Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst podtrac.com) - zu wenig fuer ein Urteil, aber nicht nichts; Ausschnitte dieser Sendung waren in zwei Messungen mit Stunden Abstand stumm - die Datei wird je Abruf neu zusammengesetzt

einzeiler: Japan's covert biological warfare unit and human experimentation program during WWII.
kurzfassung: Unit 731 was a covert biological and chemical warfare research unit of the Imperial Japanese Army that conducted horrific human experiments on prisoners of war during the Second Sino-Japanese War and WWII. Led by Shiro Ishii, the facility used thousands of prisoners as test subjects for weapons, diseases, frostbite, and vivisections without anesthesia. After the war, American authorities granted immunity to many of the perpetrators in exchange for research data, while the Soviet Union prosecuted leaders in the Khabarovsk trials.
stichpunkte: Japan maintained a long isolationist peace under the Tokugawa Shogunate, fostering a strict honor-and-shame culture that emphasized absolute obedience.
The Second Sino-Japanese War began in 1937 following years of skirmishes, resulting in massive civilian casualties and brutal military campaigns.
Shiro Ishii founded Unit 731 in Manchuria to research and develop biological and chemical weapons, operating outside the Geneva Protocol.
Thousands of prisoners, referred to as 'logs' or 'maruta', were subjected to horrific experiments, including frostbite testing, weapon trials, and deliberate disease infections.
Vivisections were routinely performed on living prisoners without anesthesia to study organ damage and disease progression.
Field tests of biological weapons contaminated water sources and spread plague-infected fleas across Chinese villages.
As Soviet forces advanced in 1945, Unit 731 personnel destroyed facilities, murdered remaining prisoners, and attempted to cover up evidence.
American occupational authorities secretly granted immunity to Shiro Ishii and other unit members in exchange for research data, shielding them from the Tokyo War Crimes Tribunal.
The Soviet Union prosecuted twelve military leaders and scientists associated with Unit 731 in the 1949 Khabarovsk War Crimes Trials.

kapitel.titel: The Rise of Shiro Ishii and Unit 731

clips.text: The host introduces two historical studies by Robert Comer and John W. Powell that cover Japanese biological weapons development between 1930 and 1945.
Shiro Ishii earned a doctorate in bacteriology, earned high-level military approval, and advanced to the rank of Army Surgeon Second Class.
Researchers tested anthrax on human subjects, incinerated the corpses in dedicated furnaces, and secured increased funding as military conflicts expanded.
Unit 731 was established to safeguard Japanese forces and injure adversaries through lethal human experimentation.

clips.hook: US grants immunity for research data
clips.text: The conversation shifts to a discussion involving guests like Sarah Sherman and Adam Scott, along with unexpected comedic mix-ups regarding Adam Sandler.

beschreibung:
Unit 731 is one of WWII's lesser known horrors. Imperial Japan's covert biological warfare research and development unit that engaged in brutal and inhumane experimentation on victims known as "logs."
These prisoners were infected with pathogens, deadly diseases from dysentery to the plague, studied and vivisected, all for the good of the Empire, and spearheaded by the sinister microbiologist Shiro Ishii.
